title: Spike: verify concurrent bd writes from N worktrees
description:
Before anything else, prove that 5 concurrent processes can safely hit the one embedded Dolt DB from 5 different git worktrees. Everything else in this epic assumes it.

Test: create 5 worktrees, run bd ready --claim simultaneously from all of them against a pool of 5 open issues, and confirm each process claims a DIFFERENT issue with no errors, no lock timeouts and no corruption. Repeat for concurrent bd close, bd note and bd create.

If direct embedded mode does not hold up, evaluate the alternatives bd already ships: the auto-started Dolt server (see the dolt-server.* entries in .beads/.gitignore), bd --global shared-server mode, and --dolt-auto-commit=batch. Record the verdict in the design field of the epic.
acceptance_criteria: 5 concurrent claims return 5 distinct issue IDs, zero errors, DB passes bd doctor afterwards. Chosen concurrency mode documented on the epic.
notes:
SPIKE RESULT: PASS, with one hard constraint discovered.

Setup: 5 git worktrees, 5 concurrent processes, embedded Dolt (mode: direct), bd 1.0.4, 16 cores.

PASS - concurrent bd ready --claim from 5 worktrees: 5 distinct issues claimed, each assigned to its own actor, all rc=0, empty stderr. The atomic claim holds under real contention. This is the pull-queue guarantee the whole design rests on.
PASS - concurrent bd note + bd close, each worker on ITS OWN issue: 10/10 rc=0, no lock errors, no timeouts.
PASS - concurrent bd create from 5 worktrees: 5 distinct IDs, no collisions.
PASS - bd resolves the main repo .beads/ from every worktree; no per-worktree setup needed.

FAIL - concurrent writes to the SAME issue silently lose data. 5 workers ran bd note against one issue; all 5 returned rc=0 but only 4 notes landed (worker 3 was lost). bd note is a read-modify-write on a text field with no locking, and the exit code does not report the loss.

VERDICT: embedded direct mode is fine at concurrency 5. No Dolt server, no --global, no --dolt-auto-commit=batch needed. bd doctor is unsupported in embedded mode, so integrity checks must use bd list/bd show instead.

RULE THIS IMPOSES ON THE DESIGN: exactly one writer per issue at any time. The architecture already gives us this (one worker owns one issue), but it must be enforced, not assumed:
- The orchestrator must never append notes to an issue while its worker is running. Retry/failure notes are written only after the worker has finished.
- The integrator writes to wave issues only after every worker in the wave has finished.
- Shared run state stays in .beads/auto/run.json, owned by the orchestrator alone. Never model shared state as a shared bead.
close_reason: Spike complete: embedded direct mode safe at concurrency 5; single-writer-per-issue rule discovered and recorded

title: Epic branch + PR handoff: merge a run into a temp branch and open a PR for human review
description:
Today a drain merges each completed issue branch straight into the base branch (main), so a run publishes itself with no human gate. Change the default so a run is staged on a temporary epic branch and handed to a human as a PR.

Behaviour:
- By default, a run over an epic (or any issue set) merges each issue branch, in dependency order, into a temporary epic branch rather than into the base branch.
- Conflicts during those merges use the model, exactly as the existing integrator does — the conflict-only role, resolve-and-stage.
- Only once every issue has merged cleanly and the gate passes on the fully merged epic branch is a PR opened against the base branch.
- The PR is the handoff point: a human reviews and merges. bd-auto never merges to base itself in this mode.
- If any issue is parked, or the gate is red on the epic branch, no PR is opened; the epic branch is left in place for inspection.

Configuration:
- On by default.
- The PR step can be turned off, in which case the epic branch is still produced and left for the human to do what they want with. Decide whether the branch-vs-base-merge behaviour is a separate switch from the PR switch.
design: Builds on internal/drain/integrate.go from beads-auto-imp-wz9.8, which already owns dependency-ordered merges, one model spawn per real conflict, one gate run on the merged result, and cleanup. The change is where the merges land (temp epic branch, not base) plus a terminal PR step. Naming for the temp branch and the PR body (issues landed, gate result, anything discovered) both need deciding. gh CLI is the obvious PR mechanism; note that pushing the epic branch is a publishing action, so it must be reconciled with the gitguard push blocks from beads-auto-imp-wz9.5.
acceptance_criteria:
- Default run merges into a temp epic branch, never into base.
- Merge order is the dependency order; conflicts invoke the model.
- PR is opened only when every issue merged clean AND the gate passed on the epic branch.
- Parked issue or red gate means no PR, epic branch preserved.
- PR step is switchable off, with the epic branch still produced.
- Tests cover: clean run opens a PR, red gate opens none, parked issue opens none, PR disabled produces the branch only.
notes:
Design decision on the switch question, resolved as two switches rather than one.

handoff.branch and handoff.pr are independent, and only in one direction:

  branch: true,  pr: true   (default)  stage on a temp epic branch, then open a PR
  branch: true,  pr: false             stage on the branch, open nothing
  branch: false, pr: false             merge straight into the base branch, as before
  branch: false, pr: true              refused at config load

Why: the two answer different questions. 'branch' is may bd-auto write to the branch you work on; 'pr' is may bd-auto publish. A repo with no remote, no gh, or a review that happens somewhere other than a forge wants the first without the second, and for it the epic branch IS the deliverable — so turning the PR off must still produce it, which is what the user's phrasing asked for and what the acceptance criteria require. The reverse is not a setting but a contradiction: a pull request needs a head branch that is not the base, so pr: true with branch: false is refused at load rather than silently resolved either way. branch: false stays as the escape hatch back to the old behaviour and turns the PR off with it. CLI equivalents are --no-pr and --no-epic-branch.

Two further calls worth recording:

- The PR is a whole-run step, not a per-barrier one. 'Only once every issue has merged cleanly' is a fact about the run, so it lives at the end of the drain (Engine.Handoff, called from finish, the run's single exit) rather than in Integrate. bd-auto integrate therefore stages and merges but never opens a PR.
- The checkout stays on the epic branch for the whole run and is left there. A worker branches from the main checkout HEAD, so moving it back between waves would hand wave two a tree with wave one missing. Switching back at the end is not attempted either: by then the tree holds the whole run and the switch would usually be refused.
close_reason: Closed

title: Swarm: bd-auto: headless engine with a swappable agent backend
description:
Swarm molecule orchestrating epic beads-auto-imp-wz9.

Epic: beads-auto-imp-wz9
Coordinator:

title: Scope selection and bd-auto drain
description:
The human bound on a run, and the wave engine that respects it.

drain does not drain an epic, it drains a set of issues a human named. There is
no automatic limit on spend anywhere in this design, so the bound is applied up
front, at the only moment the user can see what they are agreeing to.

- On a TTY: compute the candidate set (the epic's open, unparked children), show
  it with the wave decomposition, the gate commands and the model chosen per
  role, and require an explicit multi-select and confirmation. Nothing spawns
  before the confirm. It is a preview of the shape of the spend, not a yes/no.
- Off a TTY (skill launcher, CI, --plain): scope must be explicit, via
  --issues a,b,c or --epic X --all. A bare --epic X with no TTY and no explicit
  selection prints the candidate set and EXITS NON-ZERO without dispatching. The
  background path is the one with nobody watching, so it is the one that must
  name its work.
- Selected IDs go to run state as Scope before anything runs. wave.Plan
  intersects bd ready with Scope; an issue outside it is never dispatched,
  whatever bd says about its readiness.
- Discovered work is out of scope by construction: workers file it deferred, and
  a deferred issue was not in the approved list.
- An in-scope issue whose dependency is out of scope and unmet is parked
  immediately with that reason, rather than sitting unready until the run ends
  unable to explain itself.
- The run ends when every scoped issue is done or parked. The epic may still be
  open, and epicComplete refuses to close it unless every child completed.

Then the engine around it: wave loop, errgroup bounded by concurrency, event
bus, plain and --json renderers, and interrupt recovery (resume the persisted
session when the worktree survived, else fresh; attempt counter unchanged
either way).

autonomy shrinks to auto | wave. wave still pauses at each barrier and waits for
bd-auto run resume, which is useful when the scope is large. issue is deleted:
pausing after each issue is redundant when the human already chose the issues.

Interrupt recovery has one known hazard, and it is specific. A claude -p killed
mid-turn can leave a transcript ending in a tool_use block with no matching
tool_result; resuming that sends an invalid message sequence and errors
immediately. With the Class taxonomy that is an infra-failed on the first
resumed turn, which falls back to a fresh dispatch automatically. That is what
makes the least-tested path in the system self-healing rather than a coin flip.
acceptance_criteria:
- An issue outside Scope is never dispatched even when bd ready offers it.
- An in-scope issue with an unmet out-of-scope dependency parks immediately with
  that reason.
- A non-TTY drain with no explicit scope exits non-zero and spawns nothing.
- A 4-issue synthetic DAG in a temp repo with provider: fake exercises a clean
  pass, a parked issue and a full wave barrier.
- Interrupting mid-wave and re-running resumes the interrupted session; a
  resumed first turn returning infra-failed falls back to fresh without
  consuming an attempt.
- Plain and --json renderers cover everything the TUI will show.
close_reason: Closed

title: Measure resume vs fresh, then set the defaults
description:
The recovery design rests on a number nobody has measured yet, so measure it
before choosing the default rather than after.

The claim is that resuming is cheaper than a fresh worker because a fresh worker
re-reads the issue, re-explores the code and re-derives its plan first. The
counterargument, stated honestly in the plan: a resumed session re-sends its
whole transcript every turn, so its per-turn input is strictly larger. The
cache-warmth that would offset this depends on a five-minute TTL, and between
rounds we run the full gate (go build && go vet && go test) and possibly a
reviewer, which can comfortably exceed it. The transcript also grows every round
until it autocompacts, at which point the warm prefix is gone and a compaction
has been paid for.

Drain the same small epic twice with bd-auto issue run:
  max_rounds: 1, retry: 3   (fresh-heavy)
  max_rounds: 4, retry: 1   (resume-heavy)

Compare accumulated total_cost_usd, NOT token counts: cache reads bill at a
fraction of input price and a raw token count flatters whichever side reads more
cache.
acceptance_criteria:
- Both configurations run over the same epic from the same starting commit.
- The two total_cost_usd figures, the round/attempt counts and the wall-clock
  times are recorded in this issue's notes.
- max_rounds and retry defaults in config are set from the result, and
  plans/headless.md is updated to state the measured outcome rather than the
  hypothesis.
notes:
bd-auto attempt 1/2 failed at stage "implement" on 2026-08-17T06:11:35Z:
worker session terminated by API session limit before reporting; no work product
MEASURED 2026-08-17. Harness: scripts/resume-vs-fresh.sh (make resume-vs-fresh), summariser scripts/resume_vs_fresh_report.py.

Method. Both arms drain the SAME fixture epic from the SAME starting commit (fixture base 1226a508), in their own throwaway git repo with its own beads database, differing in nothing but the two knobs. The fixture forces exactly one recovery per issue: a run: pipeline stage mints a random token on its first invocation for an issue and fails, printing the line the worker must add, so no worker can pass round one and every worker can pass round two. Both arms therefore spend the SAME six model processes on the same work; the only variable is whether process two continues the session or replaces it. Confirmed from the transcripts: the resume arm reuses one session id across rounds, the fresh arm starts a new one per attempt. Task per issue: read six files under docs/ and summarise them, so the fresh attempt pays a real re-derivation rather than a token one. Model sonnet, 3 issues, pipeline implement + verify (no reviewer, to keep the round count deterministic).

RESULT (3 issues, sonnet)
| arm    | config                | done | processes | attempts | total_cost_usd | wall clock |
| fresh  | max_rounds 1, retry 3 | 3/3  | 6         | 6        | $1.7210        | 264s       |
| resume | max_rounds 4, retry 1 | 3/3  | 6         | 3        | $1.4055        | 195s       |

Resume is 18.3% cheaper and 26% faster. It won on every issue, not on one outlier:
  fresh   fx-k8n.1 $0.6361 / fx-k8n.2 $0.5139 / fx-k8n.3 $0.5710   (2 attempts, 1 round each)
  resume  fx-k8n.1 $0.3888 / fx-k8n.2 $0.5103 / fx-k8n.3 $0.5065   (1 attempt, 2 rounds each)
Zero infra retries in either arm.

Rehearsal, independent data point: 1 issue on haiku gave $0.1061 resume against $0.1648 fresh, -35.6%, and 46s against 101s.

Tokens, for completeness only (cost is the comparison; cache reads bill far below input price):
  fresh   input 144   output 15956  cache read 2969221  cache creation 98412
  resume  input 100   output  8292  cache read 1982817  cache creation 114334

The plan's counterargument was that a resumed session re-sends its whole transcript each turn, so its input is strictly larger. True per turn, wrong in aggregate: the resume arm read fewer cached tokens and produced half the output. A fresh attempt does not only re-derive its plan, it re-runs the exploration, and every tool result that produces is then re-sent on every remaining turn of the new session.

DEFAULTS SET FROM THIS. max_rounds 3, retry 1 — unchanged in value, now measured rather than assumed, and with the roles fixed the way the plan wanted: rounds primary, retry the safety net. 3 rather than 2 because the dogfood run needed three to clear a hard review; not more, because nothing past round two was measured and a long attempt eventually loses its cache prefix to the 5-minute TTL and its transcript to an autocompact. retry 1 because a fresh attempt is the only escape from a session that has gone wrong in itself. Recorded in internal/config/config.go, internal/config/template.go, .beads-auto.yaml, plans/headless.md and README.md.

LIMITS, stated. The fixture's re-derivation is six small files; a repo with heavier exploration should widen the gap, one with almost none should narrow it. Both arms ran sonnet, not the default opus, so the ratio transfers and the dollars do not. Only one recovery round per issue was exercised. The reviewer was left out of the pipeline to keep round counts deterministic, so this measures the worker loop, which is what these two knobs govern.

TWO BUGS FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT, filed deferred:
  beads-auto-imp-so5 - beads' post-checkout hook imports .beads/issues.jsonl back over the database when the next attempt's worktree is created, deleting the failure note bd-auto had just written. A fresh attempt gets no feedback in its prompt at all, so notes are its whole feedback channel; without them the fresh arm burned all four attempts repeating one mistake. Reproduced with git alone. The harness disables beads' hooks in the fixture for exactly this reason, or the experiment would have measured the bug.
  beads-auto-imp-o4q - permissions: auto, the shipped default, refused a headless worker every file write; it looped 226s and $0.41 and died on the no-progress check. The fixture uses bypass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Per-issue pipeline and bd-auto issue run --issue X
description:
One issue end to end, standalone and debuggable before any wave logic exists.
The unified recovery loop with one feedback channel:

  mark := worktree.Snapshot(wt)                    // branch tip + dirty set
  res  := runner.Run(...)
  infra-failed  -> backoff, re-run the same round  // no round, no attempt spent
  interrupted   -> return; attempt counter untouched
  !Changed      -> hard fail the attempt           // NOT another round
  !Terminal     -> feedback, next round
  guard fails   -> feedback, next round
  gate fails    -> feedback, next round
  review fails  -> feedback, next round

The progress check must come first and must be a hard failure. Every check below
it is satisfiable by stale state: after round 1 the issue is already closed, so
Terminal() passes on round 2 even if round 2 did nothing, and gitguard.Verify
passes on an unchanged branch. A no-op round would sail through to the reviewer,
which re-reads an identical diff, fails identically, and spends every remaining
round in an empty loop at full price.

Sessions persist to run state (Attempt.AgentID at state.go:38 becomes
WorkerSession and ReviewSession, written before the runner is invoked rather
than by a hook afterwards). Review notes go to .beads/auto/review/<id>.md.

The reviewer defaults to a FRESH session. Reviewer resume is available but off:
a resumed reviewer carries its own previous VERDICT: fail and is anchored to
checking whether its findings were addressed rather than re-judging the diff,
and it is the cheap half anyway since the diff dominates its input and must be
re-read after changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- bd-auto issue run --issue X drives one issue through implement, gate and review
  with resume rounds, using the fake runner in tests and claude for real.
- A gate failure, a review failure and a guard violation each produce a
  Resume: true request on the SAME session ID, with the worktree surviving.
- A round returning ok with no commit and no file change fails the attempt
  outright and does not consume the remaining rounds.
- fake returning infra-failed then ok re-runs the same round index, with neither
  the round nor the attempt counter advanced.
- A Caps().Resume == false variant reaches the same outcomes via fresh processes.
- discardAttempt fires only between attempts, never between rounds.
close_reason: Closed

title: internal/worktree and internal/gitguard: own the worktree and close the git holes
description:
Worktree creation is currently Claude Code's job via `isolation: worktree` in the
agent frontmatter. Verified: `git worktree add` appears nowhere in the Go code,
only listWorktrees (merge.go:201) and `git worktree remove` (worker.go:174).
Deleting the plugin deletes worktree creation, so Go has to own the lifecycle.

internal/worktree:
- create at .beads/auto/wt/<issue> from the base SHA recorded at dispatch
- reuse on a later round and on a resumed run. The path must be stable, because
  `claude --resume` resolves a session against the project derived from cwd; a
  moved worktree is a lost session
- `git worktree prune` at drain start, plus adopt-or-recreate for the
  "worktree exists, branch does not" case
- removal only between attempts and after a successful merge

internal/gitguard replaces the PreToolUse deny at hook.go:280, whose
agent_id == "" guard (hook.go:348) silently stops firing headless.

Structural, at worktree creation. Two traps, both confirmed against this repo:
- --worktree and extensions.worktreeConfig are BOTH required; a plain git config
  inside a worktree writes the shared config and breaks the main checkout.
- core.hooksPath is ALREADY set here, to .beads/hooks, holding beads' pre-commit,
  pre-push, post-checkout, post-merge and prepare-commit-msg. Pointing it at a
  rejector dir disables every one of them inside worker worktrees, including the
  pre-commit that keeps issues.jsonl in sync. So the rejector dir is generated
  per run and CHAINS: reject if it is one bd-auto blocks, else exec the
  same-named hook under the previous hooksPath with "$@" (falling back to
  .git/hooks). Its own prepare-commit-msg appends a Bd-Auto: <issue>/<attempt>
  trailer before chaining.

What the structural half cannot catch: pre-merge-commit does not fire on a
fast-forward merge, and git rebase has no hook at all. pre-push does fire for
every push regardless of remote, so the push half is genuinely closed once
chaining works.

Post-hoc, against the base SHA recorded at dispatch:
- git merge-base --is-ancestor <base> <branch>
- git rev-list --min-parents=2 --count <base>..<branch> is 0
- EVERY commit in <base>..<branch> carries this run's Bd-Auto: trailer
- base branch SHA unchanged
- refs/remotes/origin/* unchanged

The trailer check is the one that closes the holes. After `git rebase
origin/main` the base is still an ancestor, there are still no merge commits,
and the local and remote refs are still unchanged, but base..branch now contains
origin's commits and those have no trailer. Same for a fast-forward merge.
acceptance_criteria:
- Worktrees created, reused, pruned and removed by Go; paths stable across rounds.
- Rejector hooks chain: a test asserts beads' own pre-commit still runs inside a
  worker worktree.
- Guard tests against temp repos with a fake origin: fast-forward merge from
  origin, rebase onto origin, push, and a clean branch. The first two must be
  caught by the trailer predicate, which the shape predicates alone do not catch.
- Rejection messages say what to do instead, not only what is forbidden.
close_reason: Closed

title: runner/claude and runner/fake adapters
description:
The only shipping backend, plus the scripted adapter that makes the whole engine
testable with zero model calls.

claude -p <task> --append-system-prompt <role> --model <m> --permission-mode auto
  --session-id <uuid> | --resume <uuid>
  --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages
  --allowed-tools ...   (reviewer only)

All verified present in CLI 2.1.233. --include-partial-messages is what makes
the TUI activity line text-granular rather than tool-call-granular.

Two details that are easy to get wrong and expensive to debug:

- Cancellation must kill the process group. exec.CommandContext kills the direct
  child only, so a worker 40s into `go test ./...` leaves the test running and
  holding its worktree. Set SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true} and signal the group
  (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a grace period).
- Usage is recorded as cost, not summed tokens. Across resume rounds the same
  prefix is billed repeatedly as cache reads at a fraction of input price, so
  summing input_tokens overstates a resumed attempt. Record total_cost_usd plus
  input/output/cache-read/cache-creation separately.

fake replays scripted results including Class, and records every Request it
receives so downstream tests can assert exactly what was asked for.
acceptance_criteria:
- Table tests on constructed argv for each role, resume and fresh.
- stream-json parsing yields tool-call and text events, plus the final result.
- Exit code / stderr map to Class; a usage-limit and a 429 both map to
  infra-failed.
- Cancelling the context kills a grandchild process, asserted in a test.
- Usage carries total_cost_usd and cache-read/cache-creation separately.
- fake records every Request and can script per-call Class sequences.
close_reason: Closed

title: internal/runner: Runner interface, Class taxonomy and per-role config
description:
The seam everything else plugs into. Defines Runner, Request, Result,
Capabilities, Permissions, and the Class taxonomy the engine branches on before
anything else:

  ok | work-failed | infra-failed | interrupted

Class exists because "the process exited non-zero" is not one thing. Without it,
five parallel workers meeting one rate limit each burn three rounds and a fresh
attempt against a 429 and then park five good issues with a nonsense reason.
infra-failed must consume neither a round nor an attempt.

Also lands the runners: config block with per-role resolution over default, and
the two validation rules called out in the plan: a pipeline stage's agent: field
now names a key under runners: (a silent breaking change), and per-stage
max_rounds wins over the run-level setting.

Plan: plans/headless.md, sections "The Runner seam" and "Config".
acceptance_criteria:
- Runner, Request, Result (with Class and Err), Capabilities, Permissions defined.
- runners: block parses; per-role values resolve over default; table tests cover
  resolution including partial overrides.
- Config load fails with the list of valid roles when a stage's agent: names a
  role that is not defined.
- Per-stage max_rounds precedence over run-level max_rounds is tested.
close_reason: Closed

title: bd-auto: headless engine with a swappable agent backend
description:
Invert bd-auto: Go owns control flow and spawns models as subprocesses, instead
of a live orchestrator context dispatching subagents through the Agent tool.

Today coordination is O(issues) in one append-only transcript that is re-sent
every turn, which is the context blow-up this project exists to fix. Model
invocation goes behind a Runner interface so the backend can be swapped without
touching the engine.

What bounds a run is a human-selected set of issues, chosen before any model is
spawned. There are no budgets, no per-request timeouts and no circuit breakers.

Full plan: plans/headless.md
acceptance_criteria:
- A drain launched from a Claude Code session via the rewritten skill grows the
  launching session by under 2k tokens regardless of epic size. This is the
  number every other issue here serves.
- A run never touches an issue the human did not select.
- go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... passes at every child issue.
close_reason: 11 child issues completed, integrated and gated

title: Plan: persistent graphify-backed codebase index initialised at each wave start
description:
We need a human plan/decision before implementing.

Idea: at the start of every bd-auto wave, initialise a persistent tool/service backed by graphify (the knowledge-graph skill) over the current codebase. Worker, reviewer and integrator agents then query that tool instead of grepping and reading files, so they can understand the codebase at a much lower token count.

Open questions for the human:
- Where does the graph live (graphify-out/ in the main checkout? shared read-only mount into each worktree?) and who owns its lifecycle?
- When is it built/refreshed — once per wave at dispatch, or incrementally after the integrator merges each wave?
- How do agents query it: a slash command / skill invocation, an MCP server, or a plain CLI the agents shell out to?
- Staleness policy: worktrees diverge from the base branch during a wave, so how do we signal that graph answers may lag the worker's own edits?
- Cost/benefit: graph build time and tokens vs. the per-agent context savings. Is it worth it below some issue count?
- Fallback: what agents do when the graph is missing, stale or the build fails.

Deliverable: a written plan (design doc or a set of child issues) that a bd-auto wave can then implement.
acceptance_criteria: A human has answered the open questions and either a design doc or a set of child implementation issues exists.

title: Plugin packaging and required repo settings
description:
Package as a proper Claude Code plugin in this repo: .claude-plugin/plugin.json plus skills/, agents/, hooks/hooks.json, bin/. Load during development with claude --plugin-dir . and validate with claude plugin validate.

Repo settings this design REQUIRES, documented in the README and applied here:
- worktree.baseRef=head in settings, otherwise subagent worktrees branch from the default branch and a wave will not see the previous wave merge.
- .claude/worktrees/ added to .gitignore.
- .worktreeinclude if any gitignored file is needed inside worker worktrees. Note .beads/embeddeddolt must NOT be copied; bd already resolves the main repo database from inside a worktree.
- The session must run in an accepting permission mode. permissionMode in frontmatter is ignored for PLUGIN subagents, so five workers in a prompting mode would produce a prompt storm.
- Use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} for every hook command path.
acceptance_criteria: claude plugin validate passes. A fresh clone plus claude --plugin-dir gives a working /bd-auto. Required settings are documented and applied.
close_reason: Plugin manifest, hooks.json, Makefile, gitignore and worktree.baseRef=head; claude plugin validate passes

title: Failure policy: retry once fresh, then park
description:
Uniform handling for a worker that errors, a gate that will not pass, or a review that fails twice.

First failure: discard the attempt (remove its worktree and branch), retry the issue with a FRESH worker seeded with the failure notes appended to the issue. Second failure: bd update --status=blocked --append-notes with the accumulated evidence, flag with bd human, and continue the run. A single bad issue must never stall the drain.

Retry count is configurable. Every attempt appends to the issue notes so the history is in beads rather than in a context window that is about to be compacted.
acceptance_criteria: An issue whose gate cannot pass ends the run blocked, flagged for human review, with both attempts notes on the issue, while the remaining issues in the epic still complete.
close_reason: Retry-once-fresh-then-park implemented in bd-auto worker fail; full lifecycle smoke-tested

title: Skill and slash command: the orchestrator protocol
description:
skills/bd-auto/SKILL.md defines what the main session does: validate the DAG, start the run, compute a wave, dispatch all workers for that wave IN A SINGLE MESSAGE so they run in parallel, collect capped reports, run the review stage (resuming the same worker with feedback on rejection, max 2 rounds), hit the wave barrier, invoke the integrator, then loop.

Keep it SHORT. It is re-injected by the SessionStart/PostCompact hooks, and a long skill defeats the purpose. Anything that can be enforced by the binary or a hook does not belong in prose here.

Entry point /bd-auto <epic-id> with flags for concurrency, autonomy mode and dry run. Dry run prints the wave plan and the resolved pipeline without dispatching.
acceptance_criteria: /bd-auto <epic> --dry-run prints the wave plan and pipeline. A real run dispatches a full wave in one message and reaches the wave barrier without the user intervening.
close_reason: skills/bd-auto/SKILL.md defines the orchestrator loop, kept short because the rehydration hook re-injects it

title: Wave integrator: dependency-ordered merge with conflict resolution
description:
At each wave barrier, merge the wave branches into main.

Order the bd-auto/<id> branches by the beads dependency graph, merge in that order, resolve conflicts, and require the gate to pass on the merged result. On resolution failure or gate failure, park the offending branch, reopen its issue with notes explaining the conflict, and flag it with bd human; the rest of the wave still lands.

Consider taking bd merge-slot around the merge so this stays correct if a second orchestrator ever runs concurrently. After a branch merges cleanly, remove its worktree (git worktree remove --force) so worktrees do not accumulate.

Note: worker worktrees are git-locked while their agent runs and released when it finishes, so cleanup must happen after the worker completes, not during.
acceptance_criteria: A wave of three branches, two clean and one conflicting, results in two merged issues and one parked-and-reopened issue with notes, gate green on main, and no leftover worktrees for the merged pair.
close_reason: bd-auto merge-order with Kahn topo sort + bd-integrator agent; ordering unit-tested, branch detection smoke-tested. Conflict resolution is agent behaviour, verified by eqc.13

title: Hooks: Stop autonomy driver and compaction rehydration
description:
The two hooks that make this survive long sessions.

Stop hook: armed ONLY while .beads/auto/run.json exists, so ordinary sessions in this repo are unaffected. While a run is active and the epic still has ready work, exit 2 with a precise next instruction on stderr (dispatch wave N: <ids>). This is the autonomy engine: the orchestrator physically cannot end the turn while claimable work remains. Honours the autonomy mode: auto drains the queue, wave pauses at each wave barrier, issue pauses after every issue.

SessionStart and PostCompact hooks: when a run is active, print the run state as context. This is the direct fix for the reported problem, the model forgetting its instructions after autocompact. The existing PreCompact bd prime hook stays.

Guard against a runaway loop: cap consecutive Stop-hook continuations and stop the run with a clear message if the wave number does not advance.
acceptance_criteria: With a run active the session cannot stop while ready work remains; with no run active the Stop hook is a no-op. After a forced /compact the session recovers the epic, wave and in-flight issues without the user restating anything.
close_reason: Stop autonomy driver + SessionStart/PostCompact rehydration; decision matrix unit-tested, hooks smoke-tested

title: Agent definitions: bd-worker, bd-reviewer, bd-integrator
description:
Three subagent definitions in agents/.

bd-worker (isolation: worktree): implements exactly one issue. Protocol: bd update <id> --claim, git switch -c bd-auto/<id>, read the issue with bd show including design/acceptance/notes, implement, run the gate, commit with -m referencing the issue ID, and report a CAPPED structured footer (issue, branch, status, <=5 line summary). It closes its issue only after gate and review pass. Discovered work is filed with bd create --deps discovered-from:<id> and deferred, never worked in the current run.

bd-reviewer: read-only tools. Reviews the worker diff against the issue acceptance criteria, returns a pass/fail verdict with specific actionable notes.

bd-integrator: runs in the main checkout, merges the wave branches in dependency order, resolves conflicts, and requires the gate to pass on the merged result.

Two hard constraints go in the worker prompt: worktree-isolated agents cannot use heredocs with unquoted delimiters or brace expansion (use git commit -m and the Write tool), and the report must stay within its size budget because it is the only thing that reaches the orchestrator context.

Consider omitting Agent from bd-worker tools so workers cannot recursively spawn their own subagents and multiply token cost.
acceptance_criteria: A worker dispatched against a single real issue claims it, works in its own worktree, commits to bd-auto/<id>, and returns a report within the size budget. Reviewer returns a structured verdict. Integrator merges two branches and runs the gate.
close_reason: bd-worker (isolation: worktree), bd-reviewer (read-only) and bd-integrator defined; worktree shell constraints and report cap encoded in the worker prompt. Live agent behaviour verified by eqc.13

title: Gate runner and pipeline stage executor
description:
Execute the configured per-issue pipeline. Stages are ordered and each is either agent: <subagent-name> or run: <shell command>. The built-in stages are implement (the worker itself) and gate (the configured build/test/lint commands); everything after is user-extensible, which is how a custom code-review pipeline plugs in.

The binary owns run: stages (execute, capture exit code, capture a bounded tail of output). agent: stages are executed by the orchestrator or worker via the Agent tool, so the binary only resolves and reports them. Stage output fed back into a retry must be truncated to a fixed budget so a failing test suite cannot blow the worker context.

Expose $BD_ISSUE, $BD_BRANCH and a path to the diff as environment to run: stages.
acceptance_criteria: A repo with a two-command gate and one custom run: stage executes all stages in order, stops at the first failure, and returns a structured result naming the failing stage with a bounded output tail.
close_reason: Gate runner and stage executor with bounded output; agent stages resolved not executed

title: Wave planner: bd-auto plan
description:
Compute the next wave of issues for a run.

Reads bd ready --parent <epic> --json, intersects with the run state (excluding parked, in-flight and already-done issues), caps at the configured concurrency (default 5), and emits the wave as JSON for the orchestrator to dispatch.

Prefer delegating dependency analysis to bd rather than reimplementing it: bd ready is already blocker-aware, and bd swarm validate already reports ready fronts and max parallelism. Call bd swarm validate at run start and surface its warnings (wrong dependency direction, orphans, cycles) rather than silently running on a bad DAG.
acceptance_criteria: Returns only issues with no unresolved blockers inside the epic; never returns a parked or in-flight issue; respects the concurrency cap; emits an empty wave when the epic is drained.
close_reason: bd-auto plan / plan --dispatch; delegates readiness to bd ready; smoke-tested incl. DAG exclusion

title: Go binary skeleton: config loader and run state
description:
Create bin/bd-auto, the single Go binary that backs both the hooks and the orchestrator helper commands.

Scope: cobra-style subcommand skeleton; parse .beads-auto.yaml (gate commands, ordered pipeline stages, concurrency, autonomy mode, retry count) with defaults for every field so a repo with no config still works; implement run start/status/stop over a state file at .beads/auto/run.json holding epic ID, wave number, dispatched issues, completed, parked, and a snapshot of the resolved config.

The run state file is the mechanism that makes a run survive autocompact, so treat its schema as the contract other issues code against. All output JSON on stdout, human text on stderr, so hooks can consume it.
acceptance_criteria: bd-auto run start --epic X writes valid run.json; run status emits JSON; run stop removes the armed flag; config loads with all defaults applied when .beads-auto.yaml is absent.
close_reason: Go binary, config loader and flock-guarded run state; unit tests incl. cross-process concurrency

title: bd-auto: beads-driven subagent orchestration plugin for Claude Code
description:
Claude Code plugin that drains a beads epic by dispatching one worktree-isolated subagent per issue, in dependency-ordered waves, with a configurable per-issue pipeline (gate, review, custom stages) and an end-of-wave integrator.

Problem: long multi-step sessions blow the context window, autocompact fires, and the model forgets its instructions even though every fact needed is already in the beads issues. Fix: each issue runs in a fresh, isolated subagent context; beads holds all durable state so the orchestrator can rehydrate after compaction; disjoint issues run in parallel.

Decisions locked (see design field): in-session subagents; worktree per worker; merge at end of wave; gate command + reviewer agent + user-extensible stages; retry once fresh then park; epic-scoped runs; concurrency 5; Go single binary; Stop hook armed only during a run.
design:
ARCHITECTURE
- bin/bd-auto: single Go binary. Both the hook entrypoint and the orchestrator helper. Subcommands: run start|status|stop, plan, gate, stage, hook <event>, merge-order.
- Run state at .beads/auto/run.json (epic, wave, dispatched, done, parked, config snapshot). This is what makes the run survive autocompact.
- Hooks (hooks/hooks.json): Stop (autonomy driver, exit 2 while work remains), SessionStart + PostCompact (rehydrate run state into context), SubagentStop (verify worker reached a terminal state), PreToolUse/Bash (bind agent_id to issue via the --claim call, block workers merging into main).
- Agents (agents/*.md): bd-worker (isolation: worktree), bd-reviewer (read-only), bd-integrator (main checkout, merges the wave).
- Skill (skills/bd-auto/SKILL.md): the orchestrator dispatch protocol, kept short and re-injected by hooks so compaction cannot erase it.
- Config .beads-auto.yaml at repo root: gate commands, ordered pipeline stages (each either agent: <name> or run: <cmd>), concurrency, autonomy mode, retry count.

RUN LIFECYCLE
1. bd swarm validate <epic> for DAG sanity, then bd-auto run start.
2. Wave = bd ready --parent <epic> ready-front, capped at concurrency (default 5).
3. Dispatch N bd-worker subagents in a single message so they run in parallel.
4. Worker: bd update <id> --claim, git switch -c bd-auto/<id>, implement, gate, commit, report a capped structured footer.
5. Review stage; on reject resume the SAME worker with feedback (retains context and worktree), max 2 rounds.
6. Worker closes its issue only after gate and review pass.
7. Wave barrier: bd-integrator merges bd-auto/* branches in dependency order into main, resolves conflicts, gate must pass on the merged result. Failures reopen the issue with notes and flag bd human.
8. Repeat until bd ready --parent <epic> is empty. The Stop hook enforces the loop.

VERIFIED FACTS
- bd resolves the main repo .beads/ from inside a git worktree (bd context reports "worktree: yes"), so workers use bd normally against the one shared DB. No redirect setup needed.
- bd ready --claim is atomic, so the wave is a race-safe pull queue rather than a push assignment.
- bd swarm validate already reports ready fronts, max parallelism and dependency-direction errors.
- Hooks fire inside subagents and carry agent_id + agent_type.
- Hooks cannot spawn agents (type: agent hooks only return ok/reason), so the Stop hook drives the loop and the main session does the dispatching.

CONSTRAINTS TO DESIGN AROUND
- Worktree-isolated agents cannot run shell constructs Claude Code cannot statically trace: no heredocs with unquoted delimiters, no brace expansion. Worker prompts must use git commit -m and the Write tool.
- permissionMode in frontmatter is ignored for plugin subagents, so the run needs the session already in an accepting permission mode or 5 workers cause a prompt storm.
- Subagent worktrees branch from the default branch, not parent HEAD. Set worktree.baseRef=head so each wave sees the previous wave merge.
- No git remote on this repo: all merging is local, and the CLAUDE.md push step does not apply.
close_reason: All 13 child issues completed and merged to main; plugin is built, packaged and dogfooded (eqc.13).

title: Flaky: concurrent git worktree add fails on another worktree's commondir
description:
Seen once in a full 'go test ./...' run, in TestKillFailsOneIssueAndLeavesTheWaveRunning:

  worktree: create .../wt/t-1: git worktree add --quiet -b bd-auto/t-1 ... :
  exit status 128: fatal: failed to read .git/worktrees/t-2/commondir: Success

It did not reproduce in 8 runs of that test alone or 5 runs of the whole drain package, before or after the change it was seen on, so it looks like a pre-existing race between one goroutine running 'git worktree add' and another removing or pruning a sibling worktree in the same repo — git re-reads every entry under .git/worktrees while adding one, and a half-removed entry is what that errno-less 'Success' message is.

If it is real it affects real runs, not only tests: a wave creates and removes worktrees concurrently. Worth reproducing under a stress loop before deciding whether internal/worktree needs its own lock around add and remove.

Discovered while implementing beads-auto-imp-908.

title: bd-auto handoff: open the pull request for a run that already finished
description:
Engine.Handoff runs only from inside a drain, at finish. A run that was interrupted, or one whose parked issue a human unparked and fixed by hand, therefore has an epic branch with everything on it and no way to open the pull request short of re-running the whole drain or doing it manually with gh.

A 'bd-auto handoff [--force]' command would read the epic branch and the base out of run state, re-gate the branch, and run the same HandoffReady predicate. It is a thin wrapper over what already exists: internal/drain/handoff.go is already an exported method over a DrainReport, and the only new part is rebuilding enough of that report from run state.

Discovered while implementing beads-auto-imp-908.

title: scripts/smoke.sh cannot run in the main checkout during a drain; give it an isolated mode
description: smoke.sh refuses to start while a run is active, correctly, because its cleanup deletes .beads/auto. That means it cannot be run at all while bd-auto is draining its own epic, which is exactly when a worker changing bd-auto needs it. Verifying wz9.11 required hand-building a throwaway repo (git init, bd init --prefix, copy bin/bd-auto and scripts/smoke.sh in) and running smoke there. That harness should be part of the repo: scripts/smoke.sh --isolated, or a make target that builds the throwaway repo and runs smoke inside it. resume-vs-fresh.sh already has most of the fixture-repo code to borrow.

title: Drop the plugin-era runner role aliases (bd-worker, bd-reviewer, bd-integrator)
description: internal/config/runners.go keeps roleAliases mapping bd-worker/bd-reviewer/bd-integrator onto worker/reviewer/integrator, so configs written when those were Claude Code subagent names keep loading. The subagent definitions themselves are gone as of wz9.11. The aliases are now pure compatibility weight and a source of confusion: 'agent: bd-reviewer' reads as if it dispatches something. Removing them is a breaking change for any config still using the old names, so it wants a version bump and a note in the README, which is why it was not done inside wz9.11.

title: drain: the scope prompt can swallow keystrokes meant for the live view
description: selectInteractively wraps os.Stdin in a bufio.Reader to read the selection and the confirmation. bufio reads ahead, so anything typed after the confirming newline sits in a buffer that is discarded when the function returns — and the live view, which takes over os.Stdin immediately afterwards, never sees it. Typing ahead on a slow start therefore loses keys, including k and q. Fix by keeping one reader for the whole command and handing its buffered remainder to tui.Options.Input, or by draining stdin before the view starts.

title: permissions: auto refuses a headless worker every file write
description:
Found while building the resume-vs-fresh measurement (wz9.7).

With runners.default.permissions: auto — the shipped default — a 'claude -p' worker in a throwaway git repo was refused every Write and every shell redirect: 'Claude requested permissions to write to <path inside its own worktree>, but you haven't granted it yet.' Headless there is nobody to grant it, so the worker looped for 226 seconds and $0.41 trying alternatives (git update-index, the update-config skill, touch), changed nothing, and the attempt died on the no-progress check.

The experiment switched to permissions: bypass and the same worker wrote files immediately.

Unclear whether this reproduces in this repo's own worktrees — the temp repo may simply not have been a trusted project — but the default is 'auto', the failure mode is a whole attempt of silent flailing at full price, and no-progress reads as 'the model did nothing' rather than 'the model was not allowed to'. Worth reproducing under .beads/auto/wt/ here before a real drain relies on it.

If it does reproduce, two things are wanted: a permission denial should classify as something other than work-failed, and the default should be one that can actually write.

title: beads' post-checkout hook wipes bd-auto's failure notes, so a fresh retry starts blind
description:
Found while building the resume-vs-fresh measurement (wz9.7). Reproduced deterministically with git alone, no models involved.

A fresh attempt gets no feedback in its prompt: drain.attempt() starts each attempt with an empty feedback string, so workerPrompt renders the plain task and tells the worker to read the issue's notes. The failure notes ARE therefore the whole feedback channel for the retry path.

They do not survive. beads installs core.hooksPath=.beads/hooks, whose pre-commit EXPORTS the database to .beads/issues.jsonl and whose post-checkout IMPORTS that file back over the database. The sequence bd-auto runs is:

  1. worker commits in its worktree     -> pre-commit exports the DB to issues.jsonl on the branch
  2. the attempt fails
  3. noteFailure writes the reason to the issue  (DB only; nothing is committed)
  4. discardAttempt removes the worktree and deletes the branch, taking the exported jsonl with it
  5. worktree.Ensure creates the next attempt's worktree from base
     -> post-checkout imports the BASE jsonl over the DB, reverting everything since step 1

Step 5 deletes the note written in step 3. Verified in a throwaway repo: a note written before the worker's commit survives; a note written after it (which is where bd-auto writes) is gone the moment the next attempt's worktree is created.

Observed live first: a fresh-heavy run (max_rounds 1, retry 3) over a fixture issue burned all four attempts. The attempt-2 transcript shows the worker ran 'bd show' and got no NOTES section at all, so it repeated attempt 1's mistake exactly, three times, at full price.

Asymmetric by construction: resume rounds keep the feedback in the prompt and never re-create the worktree, so they are unaffected. Only the fresh-retry path is broken, and it fails silently — the engine's warning is discarded whenever Log is nil, which is what --quiet does.

Worth checking whether the same holds in this repo (it has the same hooks) before trusting retry to recover anything.

title: smoke.sh: cover bd-auto drain end to end with provider: fake
description:
scripts/smoke.sh still exercises only the plugin-era path (run start, plan --dispatch, worker done, merge-order). The headless drain has unit coverage but no cross-process smoke test.

Extend smoke.sh with a drain case: a throwaway epic of three trivial issues, runners.default.provider set to fake, an explicit --issues scope, and assertions that every branch merges, the epic closes, and the non-TTY refusal (bare --epic with no scope) exits non-zero having dispatched nothing.

Discovered while implementing wz9.9. The plan (plans/headless.md, Verification, Manual item 1) names this; it was left out because the acceptance criteria for wz9.9 are all covered by go test.

title: cmds/merge.go duplicates the integrator's candidate gathering
description:
internal/cmds/merge.go has its own currentBranch, commitsAhead, branchExists and listWorktrees, which internal/drain/integrate.go now also has (over internal/worktree.List). Once the plugin surface is cut (beads-auto-imp-wz9.11), merge-order should either go or be rebuilt on Engine.candidates so there is one place that decides what a mergeable candidate is.

Discovered while implementing beads-auto-imp-wz9.8.

title: Integrator: re-merge branches peeled back with a gate offender
description:
internal/drain/integrate.go blameGate peels merges back newest first to find which branch a red wave gate is about. Every branch peeled off after the offender is parked too, even though nothing is wrong with it: the work is intact on its own branch, it just is not in the merged result.

A better barrier would, once the offender is identified, re-merge the branches that were peeled with it and gate once more, parking only the offender. Cost is one extra gate run in an already-failing path.

Discovered while implementing beads-auto-imp-wz9.8.

title: bd-auto issue run creates a statusless run.json that run status reports as active
description:
The drain engine writes sessions and attempt counters through runstate.Update(create: true), so a standalone 'bd-auto issue run' with no drain around it creates .beads/auto/run.json. The created state has an empty Status, which is deliberate: runstate.Active() is false for it, so no hook is armed. But 'bd-auto run status' only special-cases ErrNoRun, so it then prints active: true with an empty epic and wave 0.

Either give run status a check for a run with no epic, or have the engine record standalone runs under a distinct status. Cosmetic, but it is the first thing anyone debugging a single issue will see.

title: Worker commits pick up .beads/issues.jsonl churn from other workers
description:
gitguard chains beads' own pre-commit hook into every worker worktree, which is correct: it keeps .beads/issues.jsonl in sync. But issues.jsonl is a tracked file exporting the SHARED dolt database, so a worker committing in its worktree stages an export reflecting every other worker's bd writes as well as its own. At concurrency 5, every branch in a wave carries a different full snapshot of the same file, and the integrator hits a conflict on it for every merge after the first.

Options: exclude .beads/issues.jsonl from worker commits via the generated rejector dir (a chained pre-commit that unstages it), have the integrator resolve that path with a regeneration rather than a merge, or drop the chain for pre-commit specifically inside worker worktrees. Verified against this repo: bd's pre-commit exported 37 issues during a normal commit here.

title: Preflight the claude CLI before a drain spends anything
description: internal/runner/claude builds argv against flags verified present in CLI 2.1.233 (--append-system-prompt, --permission-mode auto, --include-partial-messages, --session-id/--resume, --allowed-tools). An older or newer CLI that dropped or renamed one fails per-spawn, and every worker in the wave hits it separately: the failure has no result line, so it classifies as infra-failed and the engine backs off and retries an unrunnable command. A one-shot preflight at drain start -- claude --version plus a trivial -p run through the same argv builder -- would turn that into one legible error before any worktree is created. Fits alongside the scope preview in wz9.9.

title: config: validate provider: names a registered runner adapter
description: A typo in a runners: entry's provider: field loads fine and only fails when the engine is about to spawn a model, which is after worktrees have been created and a wave dispatched. runner.New already reports the known providers; internal/config could import internal/runner/providers and check provider: at load time the same way it checks a stage's agent: against the role list. Left out of wz9.2 because it changes config load behaviour, which wz9.1 owns and tested.

title: gitguard: a repo-configured pushurl survives the worktree block
description: internal/gitguard blocks pushes by setting remote.<name>.pushurl in the worktree config. pushurl is multi-valued and values accumulate across config files, so in a repo that already sets its own pushurl git pushes to that one FIRST and only then fails on bd-auto's. The pre-push hook covers this unless the worker also passes --no-verify, and gitguard.Verify's remote-moved predicate catches it after the fact. Verified against git 2.55; documented at the blockedPushScheme const. Options if this ever bites: refuse Setup when a remote already has a pushurl, or set protocol.allow=never in the worktree config (which also blocks fetch).

title: Drop the plugin-era runner role aliases
description: internal/config/runners.go carries roleAliases mapping bd-worker/bd-reviewer/bd-integrator onto the worker/reviewer/integrator roles, so configs written for the Claude Code plugin (including this repo's own .beads-auto.yaml, which still says agent: bd-reviewer) keep loading while the plugin is being cut. Once the plugin is gone (beads-auto-imp-wz9 issue 11), delete roleAliases with Config.Role's alias branch and its tests, and change .beads-auto.yaml to agent: reviewer.

title: Cut the plugin surface
description:
Deliberately last: everything it deletes stays working until the replacement is
proven.

Delete:
- hooks/ and agents/
- internal/cmds/hook.go and its tests
- the Continuations / maxContinuations autonomy engine (hook.go:25)
- Bindings from run state
- autonomy: issue

Keep .claude-plugin/plugin.json. It costs nothing and keeps the skill
installable rather than a file users copy to .claude/skills/bd-auto/SKILL.md.

Rewrite SKILL.md as a launcher: it must name its scope (--issues or --all,
never a bare epic off a TTY), run bd-auto drain --plain in the background, and
poll bd-auto run status. This is where the whole project's acceptance criterion
is actually met, so measure it here: the launching session must grow by under 2k
tokens regardless of epic size.

Update README.md and .beads-auto.yaml to the new config shape, including the
runners: block, the agent:-names-a-runner-role change, and the removal of
autonomy: issue.
acceptance_criteria:
- go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... passes with hooks.go and its
  tests gone.
- No reference to Bindings, Continuations, maxContinuations or autonomy: issue
  remains in code, config or docs.
- .claude-plugin/plugin.json still present and the plugin still installs.
- A drain launched through the rewritten SKILL.md grows the launching session by
  under 2k tokens, measured and recorded in this issue.
- scripts/smoke.sh passes against the new command surface.
notes:
Launch-cost measurement (acceptance criterion 4), reproducible with 'make launch-cost' / scripts/launch-cost.sh.

A drain launched through the rewritten SKILL.md costs the launching session
1805 tokens for a six-hour run, at any epic size:

  term                             bytes  tokens
  skill body (SKILL.md)             2379     679
  launch tool call                   200      57
  final report                       500     142
    fixed subtotal                  3079     879
  per hour of run (one poll)         540     154
  x 6 hours                         3240     925
  total                             6319    1805

Method: byte counts at 3.5 bytes/token, chosen to err high (Claude's tokenizer
averages nearer 3.8 on markdown prose). No term contains an issue count. The
skill body is fixed; the poll view is capped at 400 bytes by maxNamed=4 in
internal/cmds/run.go, asserted at 8, 400 and 4000 issues by
TestRenderContextIsBoundedByEpicSize; the poll count follows the wall clock,
not the issue count, because 'run status --wait 1h' blocks for an hour per call
instead of a sleep-and-poll loop.

The 2000-token budget therefore buys a 7-hour run at the poll view's worst case
(both named lists saturated with long IDs) and a 10-hour run at what a typical
run at concurrency 5 with nothing parked actually prints. launch-cost.sh exits
non-zero if the figure passes 2000.

Two design changes were needed to reach it: 'run status --context' was rewritten
from the plugin-era rehydration block (which listed every in-flight and parked
issue in full) into a four-line capped poll view, and 'run status --wait'
was added so one call covers an hour of run rather than one poll.

scripts/smoke.sh passes against the new command surface. It cannot run in the
main checkout during a live drain (it refuses, by design), so it was verified in
a throwaway git repo with its own beads DB: 62 checks, SMOKE PASSED.
close_reason: Closed

title: TUI: live wave view with working stop controls
description:
bubbletea + lipgloss wave table over the event stream from the drain engine:
live per-worker activity (text-granular, which is what --include-partial-messages
buys), accumulated cost per issue and for the run, and wave/attempt state.

Plus the control channel, which ships in the same issue because it is the only
way to abandon a run in flight: k kills the selected worker, q / ctrl-c stops
the run with state intact. Both depend on the process-group kill from the claude
adapter; killing the direct child only would leave a go test running and its
worktree held.

Cost is displayed, never enforced. Nothing here is a budget. With scope chosen
up front the run is already bounded; this is so you can watch it and change your
mind.

Non-TTY falls back to the plain renderer from the drain issue.
acceptance_criteria:
- Live wave table with per-worker activity, per-issue and run-total cost.
- k kills the selected worker: the process AND its children die, and the issue is
  recorded failed.
- q stops the run with state intact; re-running drain resumes the interrupted
  issue rather than restarting it.
- Non-TTY falls back to the plain renderer with no TUI code on the path.
close_reason: Closed

title: Go-driven integrator and a scope-aware epicComplete
acceptance_criteria:
- Clean merges never spawn a model; a conflicting merge spawns exactly one.
- The gate runs once on the merged result; a red result parks the offending
  branch rather than closing anything.
- epicComplete table test covers: all children done (close), one child parked
  (do not close), scope was a subset with other children open (do not close),
  and something still in flight (do not close).
close_reason: Go-driven integrator in internal/drain/integrate.go plus a tested, scope-aware EpicComplete; bd-auto integrate drives it. Gate green.

title: internal/wave: extract plan and merge-order logic out of cmds
description:
Pure refactor, no behaviour change. Lift the wave-planning logic from
cmds/plan.go and the merge ordering (topoOrder, merge.go:105) from cmds/merge.go
into callable functions returning structs, so the drain engine can use them
without shelling out to itself. The CLI commands become thin wrappers.

Doing this as its own issue keeps the behaviour-changing work downstream honest:
if the existing tests need editing, something changed that should not have.
acceptance_criteria:
- internal/wave exposes plan and merge-order as functions over explicit inputs.
- cmds/plan.go and cmds/merge.go call into it and only handle flags and JSON.
- Existing tests in internal/cmds pass untouched.
close_reason: Closed

title: prompts/: rewrite the three role prompts for headless execution
description:
agents/*.md are subagent definitions, not role prompts, and converting them is a
rewrite rather than a frontmatter strip.

bd-worker.md alone carries: the BD-AUTO: footer protocol (hook.go:215, being
deleted), "your report is the only thing that reaches the orchestrator" and its
25-line cap (there is no orchestrator context left to protect), "a hook blocks
those anyway" (there is no hook), and a Shell section about Claude Code refusing
statically unverifiable commands under worktree isolation, which does not apply
to a plain claude -p in a plain worktree.

Every role prompt also gains an explicit override of the repo's own CLAUDE.md,
which says "Work is NOT complete until git push succeeds... NEVER stop before
pushing." A headless claude -p loads CLAUDE.md exactly like an interactive
session. Today the PreToolUse deny answers that with an actionable message;
afterwards the worker gets a bare git hook rejection and, told push is
mandatory, retries or reaches for git pull --rebase, which is the rebase hole
gitguard has to close. The prompt says in as many words: you are one attempt
inside a bd-auto run, you commit to your own branch and stop, the integrator
merges, nothing here pushes.

Early on purpose: issues from the pipeline onward cannot spawn anything without
these.
acceptance_criteria:
- prompts/worker.md, prompts/reviewer.md, prompts/integrator.md exist with no
  frontmatter and no subagent-era protocol (no footer, no report cap, no
  references to hooks or the orchestrator).
- Each states explicitly that the repo CLAUDE.md push/session-completion rules
  do not apply to it and why.
- agents/*.md left in place; deletion belongs to the plugin-cut issue.
close_reason: Closed

title: Multi-worker dogfood: watch a 3-4 issue parallel wave with a real merge conflict
description:
The eqc.13 dogfood run drained a real epic with the plugin loaded, but wave 1 was a single issue, so the parallel path was never watched live. Deterministic coverage exists in make smoke; agent behaviour under contention does not.

Set up a throwaway epic of 3-4 genuinely independent issues, at least two of which touch the same file so the integrator meets a real conflict. Run with --autonomy wave so there is a barrier to inspect.

Watch for: several workers holding worktrees at once, the reviewer's send-back loop retaining worker context, the integrator resolving a genuine conflict, retry-then-park end to end, and whether the Stop hook holds the orchestrator on task across a real autocompact.

Measure: orchestrator context growth per issue (the number eqc.13 could not observe from inside a worker), and wall clock against a sequential baseline. Fold the numbers into the README's dogfood section, which currently states plainly that these are unproven.

title: Dogfood run: drain a real epic with the plugin loaded
description:
Point the finished tool at a real epic in this repo and let it drain, with the author watching. Record what actually happened: orchestrator context growth per issue, wall-clock versus a sequential baseline, how many issues needed a retry, how many merges conflicted.

Write the README from that run rather than from the design: install, config reference for .beads-auto.yaml, how to add a custom pipeline stage, how to stop a run, and how to recover a parked issue.

This epic is itself the natural first target once enough of the pipeline exists.
acceptance_criteria: One epic drained end to end without manual intervention beyond approvals, with measurements recorded on this issue and a README a stranger could follow.
notes:
README is written and committed (install, config reference, custom stage guide, required repo settings, failure handling, design notes).

What remains is the live run, which cannot be done from inside an ordinary session because it needs the plugin loaded:

  make build
  claude --plugin-dir /home/dude-lt/dev/beads-auto-imp
  /bd-auto <epic-id>

Everything below is deterministic and already covered by `make check` (unit) and `make smoke` (end to end against a throwaway epic): run state, wave planning, DAG exclusion, all five hooks, retry-then-park, merge ordering, rehydration.

What only a live run can verify, because it is agent behaviour rather than code:
- a bd-worker actually staying inside its worktree and its report budget
- bd-reviewer verdict quality and the send-back-to-same-worker loop
- bd-integrator resolving a genuine merge conflict between two workers
- whether the Stop hook keeps the orchestrator on task across a real autocompact

Measure during the run: orchestrator context growth per issue, wall clock vs a sequential baseline, retries needed, merges that conflicted. Record the numbers here and fold anything surprising back into the README.

Suggested first target: a small epic of 3-4 genuinely independent issues. Start with --autonomy wave so there is a barrier to inspect before it drains further.
DOGFOOD RUN, 2026-08-14 14:23 UTC. Epic beads-auto-imp-eqc drained with the plugin loaded (concurrency 5, autonomy auto). 12 of 13 children were already closed, so wave 1 was a single issue: this one. The worker implementing it ran under the orchestrator it was documenting.

MEASURED
- orchestrator overhead, run start to wave 1 dispatched: 8s (14:23:19 -> 14:23:27)
- retries: 0 | parked: 0 | merge conflicts: 0 (one branch in the wave)
- manual intervention: none beyond permission approvals
- orchestrator context growth per issue: not observable from inside the worker. The per-issue cost the design controls is the capped worker report; measuring real growth needs the multi-worker run filed as discovered work.

VERIFIED LIVE, not by test double
- PreToolUse binding recorded agent a42782c5c6276e01e -> eqc.13 from the worker's own claim call, with nothing passed in naming the issue.
- The integration guard denied a real integration command typed by a real worker.
- bd resolved the main repo DB from inside the worktree with no setup; show/create/close/delete all worked.
- The gate ran green inside the worktree.

NOT PROVEN BY A ONE-ISSUE WAVE
parallel workers under contention, the integrator resolving a genuine conflict, the reviewer send-back loop, retry-then-park, and the Stop hook across a real autocompact. All are covered deterministically by make smoke; none has been watched with several real agents in flight.

DEFECTS FOUND BY DOGFOODING, all fixed on this branch
1. No way to retry a parked issue. Parking excludes via run state, not just bd status, so reopening in bd alone did nothing and recovery meant hand-editing run.json. Added: bd-auto run unpark --issue <id>.
2. scripts/smoke.sh would have destroyed this live run. Its cleanup stops the run and deletes .beads/auto, and run state is shared with the main checkout even from a worktree. It now refuses while a run is active, and both preflight checks moved above the EXIT trap so bailing out no longer runs cleanup.
3. The integration guard matched its pattern anywhere in the command string, so writing this very note was denied for quoting an integration command. Now anchored to command position. This is what blocked the first attempt to record these measurements.
4. Worktree isolation is stricter than documented: a worker cannot cd to the main checkout for any git command, and a plain five-command chain is refused as unverifiable.
5. bd-auto on a worker's PATH is the main checkout's binary, i.e. the running orchestrator's build. A worker changing bd-auto must invoke ./bin/bd-auto or it silently tests the old binary.

README updated with all of the above, plus how to stop a run and how to recover a parked issue.
CORRECTION after review. Defect 3 above says the integration guard was fixed by anchoring the match to command position. That fix was wrong and is superseded: anchoring closed the false positive but opened real bypasses (a sudo prefix, an env assignment prefix, nohup, a loop body, an if condition), any of which would have let a worker integrate. The guard now keeps the original anywhere-match and blanks out single- and double-quoted spans before applying it, so quoted text is treated as data without narrowing what counts as a command. All five bypasses are in the blocked table and were checked against the built binary, not only in unit tests.

Also from review: the new unpark steps in scripts/smoke.sh had made the parked-rendering assertion vacuous, because they returned the issue to the run before the rehydration check and the bare ID then matched the in-flight line. The unpark steps moved below that check, which now asserts the literal parked-line prefix and also verifies the line disappears once the issue is unparked.
SECOND CORRECTION, final review round. Blanking quoted spans was itself unsound in two ways, both caught in review and both letting a worker integrate: executor forms (eval, xargs, and the -c form of sh and its variants) run their quoted payload, so blanking it hid the payload; and an unbalanced quote blanked everything to end of input, where an apostrophe in a trailing # comment was enough to hide the next line that the shell still runs. The guard now falls back to matching the raw command in both cases, and the strip helper reports whether it ended inside a quote instead of silently returning a truncated string. The original quoted-note case still passes.

Worth recording as a dogfood lesson: three review rounds on this one guard, each fix opening the opposite hole. Round 1 over-fired on quoted data; round 2 anchored to command position and let sudo, env, nohup, loops and if-conditions through; round 3 stripped quotes and let executors and unbalanced quotes through. A guard whose input is an arbitrary shell string has no clean regex answer, only a deliberate bias. The bias chosen here is to fall back to the broadest match whenever the parse is uncertain, since a false positive costs one rephrasing and a false negative costs an unreviewed merge.

title: PreToolUse hook: agent-to-issue binding and merge guard
description:
PreToolUse hooks fire inside subagents and carry agent_id and agent_type. Match on Bash and inspect the command.

Binding: when a worker runs bd update <id> --claim or bd ready --claim, record agent_id -> issue in the run state. That mapping is what lets SubagentStop verify the right issue and what would later enable per-worker file-ownership rules.

Merge guard: deny a worker any git merge, rebase onto main, or push. Only the integrator merges, and only at the wave barrier. Denying this deterministically is far more reliable than asking the worker not to.
acceptance_criteria: After a worker claims, run state contains its agent_id -> issue binding. A worker attempting git merge main is denied with an explanatory reason; the integrator is not.
close_reason: PreToolUse claim binding + merge guard; regexes unit-tested, both paths smoke-tested

title: SubagentStop verification hook
description:
When a worker finishes, independently verify it actually reached a terminal state rather than trusting its report: the issue is closed, or blocked with notes, and a bd-auto/<id> branch exists with a commit. If not, exit 2 to keep the worker running with a precise reason.

This closes the gap where an agent announces success without having done the bookkeeping. Depends on knowing which issue the finishing agent owned, which is what the PreToolUse claim-binding issue provides; fall back to parsing the required report footer when no binding exists.
acceptance_criteria: A worker that reports done without closing its issue is sent back with a specific reason instead of being accepted.
close_reason: SubagentStop verification incl. footer fallback and fail-open; smoke-tested all four paths

title: Configure the beads Dolt remote for cross-machine issue sync
description:
A git remote now exists (github.com/Sean-McConnachie/beads-auto-imp), but bd has its own separate Dolt remote which is not configured, so `bd dolt push` is a no-op with setup instructions.

Issue data is not currently at risk: the pre-commit hook exports .beads/issues.jsonl, which is tracked and pushed with the code. This is about live cross-machine sync, not backup.

To set up:
  bd dolt remote add origin git+ssh://git@github.com/Sean-McConnachie/beads-auto-imp.git
  bd dolt push

Left to the repo owner because it needs an SSH-based URL and their credentials.
